thread:
alex: quick sync — i spun up a small spike to compare full trace envelopes vs a compact header with external attribute lookup. main tradeoff: envelope size (cost/egress) vs query-time joins and late-enrich complexity.

riya: tl;dr numbers? how much size saving did you see?

alex: raw numbers: typical full envelope ~1.2KB, compact ~260B (ids + minimal routing attrs). ~78% reduction on avg. depends on sampled spans that carry big attrs.

ben: huge! but how much extra work at query time? we lose pre-joined attributes like tenant/display_name/etc.

alex: right. spike shows query-time ops go up — simple single-span queries add ~6-10ms for a lookup to the attr-store; multi-span reconstruction with late-enrich adds 10–25ms depending on fanout.

sophie: are those lookups cacheable? if we add a small LRU for recent tenant metadata probably most queries hit.

alex: yes, with an in-process 10k entry cache hit rate ~95% in our test workload — that knocks latency overhead to ~1–3ms.

matt: what's the impact on analytics/backfill pipelines that assume full envelope? do we need to change downstream aggregation?

alex: pipelines that run offline still need enrichment. options: (A) enrich at ingest for those events (higher ingest cost, easier queries), (B) keep compact envelope and enrich during pipeline processing (adds join step but centralized compute handles it), (C) hybrid: add a small, cheap attribute envelope for high-cardinality keys.

ben: hybrid sounds promising — keep small hot-path attrs (billing_key, tenant_id, model_id) inline, everything else via lookup. That keeps most queries cheap and trims biggest fields.

riya: question on cost attribution: if we compact envelopes and postpone enrichment, how do we ensure accurate per-tenant cost bucketing in near-real-time dashboards?

alex: for near-RT, we can materialize a condensed cost key at ingest (billing_key + token_count + model_slug) so chargeable metrics are available immediately. detailed labels for query/obs can be attached later.

observ-bot: deploy-bot: artifact built for spike-envelopes (sha: a1b2c3). Deployed to staging. :white_check_mark:

sophie: +1 to materializing just enough to do billing. otherwise we re-run large backfills.

matt: regression risk: if lookup service is down, how do we degrade? fallback to attribute bloom? or reject?

alex: plan: 1) make lookup service resilient (replicated reads + cache + circuit breaker). 2) fallback: annotate with 'attr_missing' tag and route to a low-priority enrich queue. 3) expose a degraded-metrics dashboard so teams know when labels are partial.

ben: perf tests we should run: spike with cache warm, cold start, lookup-service failure, and heavy fanout reconstruction. also measure cost delta (egress + storage) across 30-day window.

riya: i'll own the experiment matrix and run the fanout tests. alex can you share the compact envelope schema you used?

alex: pasted below — compact fields intentionally terse:

```json
{"v":1, "tid":"t-12345", "bk":"billing_01", "m":"gptx-3", "ts":1712345600, "spans": [ {"id":"s1","p":"p0","t":35} ]}
```

alex: compare to full envelope example where "attrs" is an object with 30+ keys per span.

riya: perfect. i'll start with staging runs using that schema and validate cache hit rates.

sophie: can we define the hot-attr list (the small inline set) as a feature-flag so we can iterate without schema churn?

alex: yes — feature flag + ingest config. we'll ship an initial default hot list: [billing_key, tenant_id, model_id, token_count]. teams can opt-in to add more.

matt: ok next steps summary: riya runs perf matrix, ben owns fallback strategy for query enrich, sophie owns feature-flag rollout plan, alex will harden lookup service and produce an RFC for storage/egress savings estimate. i'll schedule an hour follow-up next week.

ben: +1

riya: on it. will post results in this thread.

alex: thanks all — aim is to reduce cost without surprising product dashboards. if this looks stable we'll propose compact-envelopes as default for sampled traces. :rocket:
